messages:
jason: Heads-up — we're still seeing billing mismatches for customers with nested org/team hierarchies. I want to propose decoupling raw ingest attribution from final billing by adding an append-only accounting ledger that stores immutable token events + a separate attribution resolver. Thoughts?

maria: Do you mean a new service or just a schema change? curious about latency impact for hosted API.

jason: New lightweight service. Idea: ingest writes a minimal event to ledger synchronously (fast append), attribution resolution (owner/team/cost-center) happens async. This separates availability of token counts from correctness of attribution.

jason: Sketch of ledger event (example):
```
{
  "event_id": "uuid",
  "source_ts": 1718234567,
  "model": "gpt-x",
  "tokens": 120,
  "org_id": "org_123",
  "owner_path": ["org_123", "team_7"], // best-effort at ingest
  "attribution_pointer": "att_456", // resolves later to canonical owner(s)
  "sealed": false
}
```

sophie: How do we handle backfills / audits? if attribution changes later we need a clear replay path to update invoices.

jason: Ledger is append-only. When resolver finalizes attribution it emits a finalization event that references event_id + canonical attribution. Reconciler picks those up and emits billing adjustments (idempotent). Backfills = replay finalization events into reconciler.

alex: Two runtime concerns: 1) tail-latency for callers waiting for attribution? 2) explosion of reconciliation work if many small events change owners.

jason: 1) caller path remains fast: we only append minimal event and return. Attribution is async so no extra tail. 2) we mitigate via batching + attribution stable-window heuristics (e.g., 5m tag-resolution window) and compacted aggregation keys for hot customers.

rachel: For chargebacks/refunds we need immutable provenance and a clear correction protocol. Are we going to store both original and corrected ledger rows?

jason: yes — ledger holds originals. Corrections are new ledger rows that reference the original event_id and a correction reason. Reconciler applies delta semantics; invoice layer consumes reconciled aggregates.

maria: Observability ask: we need per-tenant lag metric and counts of unresolved events + age histogram. Also alert thresholds when unresolved > X or 95th pct age > Y.

jason: Agreed — plan: expose metrics from resolver + reconciler, per-model and per-tenant. Add per-route SLO for "attribution-finalized" within N minutes.

sophie: What about multi-attribution (event split across cost-centers)? e.g., prompt used by cross-team billing (shared feature).

jason: Ledger supports fractional attribution via attribution entries: resolver can emit multiple attribution records per event with percentages. Reconciler materializes those into charge lines.

alex: Implementation Q: where does ledger live? Kinesis/stream + compacted topic (Kafka) and a small RocksDB index? or a DB?

jason: Preference: append stream (kafka/pulsar) for durability + small write-optimized store (clickhouse/rocksdb) for queries. Keep index light — we want cheap appends.

rachel: Retention policy? audits need 1–2 years of raw events for legal/regulatory in some customers. That seems heavy on storage.

jason: Store hot recent window in the primary store (90d), then cold archive to S3 with manifest for audit retrieval. Reconciler must support rehydration from archive for legal audits.

maria: Who will own the RFC + PoC?

jason: Action items: 1) I'll draft RFC by EOW (owner: jason). 2) PoC (kafka stream + simple resolver) — sophie + alex pair. 3) Metrics + alert spec — maria. 4) Ops runbook + archive plan — rachel.

metering-bot: ingest-rate-notice: current peak ingestion ~5k events/sec, average 800 eps — size estimate for 90d hot window ~ 6TB/day raw -> need compaction.

jason: good catch. compaction + aggregation strategy is mandatory. we'll include early estimates in the RFC. thanks all :thumbsup:
